info.name: OpenG2P Master Data Service (MDS) Complete API Suite
info.description:
Comprehensive Postman Collection covering 100% of the OpenG2P Master Data Service (MDS) APIs:

1. **Authentication & Tokens**: Keycloak M2M Client Credentials and User Password Grants for Maker/Checker organizational hierarchy.
2. **Public Open Catalogue**: DCAT-3 JSON-LD discovery, public datasets, SKOS concepts, CSV/GeoJSON exports, geography boundaries.
3. **Catalogue Datasets & Metadata**: List registry, schemas, domains, ownership.
4. **Maker-Checker Governance**: Four-eyes approval workflows (draft creation, submission, review, approval/rejection, change tracking).
5. **Dataset Values & Entries**: Querying, versioning, batch upserts, retirement.
6. **Administrative Geography**: Hierarchy from National (l0) down to Woreda (l3), polygon boundaries, crosswalks.
7. **Catalogue Releases**: Version pinning and release packaging for agricultural data.
8. **Legacy & Extension APIs**: Backward compatible Attributes and Geo endpoints.

item.name: 00. Authentication & Tokens
item.description: Keycloak Token endpoints for Machine-to-Machine (M2M) and User-based Maker/Checker access.

request.description: Acquire M2M token for Registry-to-Registry / Partner Manager integration using master-data client.
Authenticate as Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) Maker to create and edit Crops, Seeds, and Fertilizer drafts.
Authenticate as MoA Checker to review, approve, or reject MoA catalog drafts.
Authenticate as Livestock Development Institute (LDI) Specialist.
Authenticate as Central Statistical Agency (CSA) Admin to manage administrative geography and boundaries.

Returns "pong" always, if the service is healthy.
This can also used for service health checks.

item.name: 03. Catalogue - Datasets & Metadata
item.description: Endpoints in group 03. Catalogue - Datasets & Metadata

request.description:
Registers a new list (code, label, labels per locale, description, owner_org, domain, visibility (private by default), licence_uri / licence_label, hierarchy flag, attribute_schema) and opens its first draft (version 1). Nothing is published until that draft is submitted and approved. `attribute_schema` is a JSON Schema (2020-12) for each value's `attributes`; a property may carry `"x-list-ref": "<LIST_CODE>"` (its value is a code of that list), and so may the `items` of an array property (a list of codes, e.g. `{"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "x-list-ref": "CROP_GROUP"}}`).

Permission: `referenceData:create`

item.name: POST /catalogue/get_catalogue_config - How this catalogue is configured

request.description:
`approval_mode` (permission | awe — the UI shows approve/reject buttons only in permission mode), whether boundary upload, audit and WebSub are enabled, the country, the geography version currently in effect and whether the anonymous /public catalogue is enabled (with its base URL).

Permission: any authenticated caller.

item.name: POST /catalogue/get_list - One dataset at a version

request.description:
A list's metadata as it is in the selected version (code, labels, attribute schema), plus that version's metadata.

Version selection: `version` (number, `"latest"` — the default, the latest published version already in effect — or `"draft"`), `as_of` (date-time: the published version in effect then) or `release` (a catalogue release code). The response's `version` object says which version answered.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

Every dataset (list) with its owner, domain (shown as Theme: `core`, `agriculture`, ...; null when unknown), visibility, licence, current published version (in effect now), highest published version (may be future-effective), open draft (number and status) and a summary of its attribute schema (properties, required, list references).

Permission: any authenticated caller.

`description`, `owner_org`, `domain`, `visibility` and `licence_uri` / `licence_label` are administrative and apply at once. `new_list_code`, `display`, `display_i18n`, `is_hierarchical` and `attribute_schema` are part of what consumers see, so they go into the open draft.

Edits only ever touch the open DRAFT (one per list / for geography); a draft is created from the highest published version when none is open. Published versions are immutable (enforced in Postgres).

Permission: `referenceData:edit`

item.name: 04. Catalogue - Drafts & Four-Eyes Governance (Maker-Checker)
item.description: Endpoints in group 04. Catalogue - Drafts & Four-Eyes Governance (Maker-Checker)

request.description:
Publishes the SUBMITTED version: it becomes immutable, `effective_from` defaults to now (or the draft's / this call's date, possibly future), and — if in effect — the legacy /attributes tables are refreshed in the same transaction. Maker ≠ checker: the approver must not have created, edited or submitted the draft (G2P-CAT-403). Disabled in awe mode.

Permission: `referenceData:publish`

Opens the list's draft as a copy of the highest published version (its base). `copy_from_version` copies another version's content instead (e.g. a REJECTED draft to rework). Optional `change_note` and `effective_from` (may be in the future). 409 if a draft is open.

Permission: `referenceData:edit`

Closes the open draft (DRAFT, or SUBMITTED in permission mode) as DISCARDED. The version row is kept so its number is never reused; the next draft gets the next number. Published versions are untouched.

Permission: `referenceData:edit`

Catalogue lifecycle events in order, from the append-only change log: list.created, list.updated, list.draft.created, list.draft.values_changed, list.draft.values_retired, list.draft.submitted, list.approval.requested, list.draft.approved, list.draft.rejected, list.version.published, list.version.effective, list.version.migrated, list.draft.discarded (and the geo.* equivalents, release.created / members_set / published / deleted). Pass the returned `next_cursor` as `cursor` to continue; `has_more` says whether to call again. Filter by `subject_type`, `subject_id`, `event_types`; `newest: true` returns the newest `limit` events instead (a recent-activity view). `actor` is the stable user id (token sub) or a system name, `actor_name` a user's display name. Every event — including those written by the database (`*.version.effective`, `*.version.migrated`) and the country-pack loader — is relayed to the Audit Manager when configured, and `*.version.published`, `*.version.effective` and `release.published` to the WebSub hub, with retries.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

`added`, `changed` (per field before/after), `retired` and `reactivated` values, and `metadata_changes` (code, label, labels, hierarchy flag, attribute schema) from `from_version` (default: the base of `to_version`) to `to_version` (number, "latest" or "draft"; default "latest"). Use `to_version: "draft"` to review a draft.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

item.name: POST /catalogue/reject_draft - Reject the submitted draft (permission mode)

request.description:
Marks the SUBMITTED version REJECTED with a required `decision_note`. Maker ≠ checker. Rework it with create_list_draft + copy_from_version.

Permission: `referenceData:publish`

item.name: POST /catalogue/retire_draft_units - Retire units in the geography draft

request.description:
Units of the base version become RETIRED (never deleted); units added in this draft are removed. Active descendants block unless `cascade`.

Edits only ever touch the open DRAFT (one per list / for geography); a draft is created from the highest published version when none is open. Published versions are immutable (enforced in Postgres).

Permission: `geo:delete`

item.name: POST /catalogue/submit_draft - Submit the draft for approval

request.description:
Validates the draft (labels, hierarchy, attribute schema and every value's typed attributes incl. list references; must differ from its base) and moves it to SUBMITTED. In awe mode this also opens an AWE approval request (policy `awe_policy_key_list`, artifact `master_data.list_version`, context incl. owner_org) and records its id in `approval_ref`.

Permission: `referenceData:edit`

item.name: POST /catalogue/update_list_draft - Set a draft's change note / effective date

request.description:
`effective_from` may not be earlier than the latest published version's.

Permission: `referenceData:edit`

item.name: POST /catalogue/upload_draft_boundary - Upload a level's boundary GeoJSON to the draft

request.description:
Stores the FeatureCollection in MinIO/S3 under the draft's key `geo/<country>/v<draft>/<level>.geojson` (never a published version's key) and records it on the draft; it becomes immutable on publish. Units whose geometry changed (features keyed by `properties.pcode`) get a BOUNDARY_CHANGE event at submit. Needs the boundary store configured.

Permission: `geo:edit`

item.name: POST /catalogue/upsert_draft_levels - Add or change levels in the geography draft

request.description:
Matched on level_id. Mnemonics must be unique under the same parent level.

Edits only ever touch the open DRAFT (one per list / for geography); a draft is created from the highest published version when none is open. Published versions are immutable (enforced in Postgres).

Permission: `geo:edit`

item.name: POST /catalogue/upsert_draft_units - Add or change units in the geography draft (batch)

request.description:
Matched on unit_id (P-code). A unit's parent must be an active unit of the parent level; names are unique among siblings. Upserting a retired unit re-activates it. Renames, re-parenting and new units get change events automatically at submit unless you record them.

Edits only ever touch the open DRAFT (one per list / for geography); a draft is created from the highest published version when none is open. Published versions are immutable (enforced in Postgres).

Permission: `geo:edit`

item.name: 05. Catalogue - Dataset Values / Entries
item.description: Endpoints in group 05. Catalogue - Dataset Values / Entries

item.name: POST /catalogue/get_list_value - One entry by code at a version

request.description:
Resolves a code in the selected version — including a RETIRED value, so an old reference still resolves against the version it was taken from.

Version selection: `version` (number, `"latest"` — the default, the latest published version already in effect — or `"draft"`), `as_of` (date-time: the published version in effect then) or `release` (a catalogue release code). The response's `version` object says which version answered.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

item.name: POST /catalogue/get_list_values - Entries (values) of a dataset at a version

request.description:
Values of the selected version, ordered by sort_order. Active values only unless `include_retired`. Filters: `parent_code` ("" = top level), `attribute_filters` (JSON containment on the typed attributes), `search` (code or label). Paged with `pagination_request`. ATTRIBUTE data policies apply as on /attributes/get_attribute_values. Response: `{list_code, version: {version_no, status, effective_from, published_at, is_latest, ...}, values: [{value_id, value_code, display, display_i18n, parent_code, sort_order, attributes, roles, status}], total}`.

Version selection: `version` (number, `"latest"` — the default, the latest published version already in effect — or `"draft"`), `as_of` (date-time: the published version in effect then) or `release` (a catalogue release code). The response's `version` object says which version answered.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

item.name: POST /catalogue/get_list_versions - Version history of a dataset

request.description:
All versions, newest first: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, PUBLISHED (with effective_from, published_at, decided_by), REJECTED (with decision_note) and DISCARDED. Numbers are never reused. `is_latest` marks the version in effect now. `*_by` fields hold stable user ids (token `sub`) or a system name; `*_by_name` the user's display name (null for a system actor).

Permission: any authenticated caller.

item.name: POST /catalogue/retire_draft_values - Retire entries in the draft

request.description:
A value that exists in the base version becomes RETIRED (kept, so old references still resolve); a value added in this draft is removed. Active children block unless `cascade`.

Edits only ever touch the open DRAFT (one per list / for geography); a draft is created from the highest published version when none is open. Published versions are immutable (enforced in Postgres).

Permission: `referenceData:delete`

item.name: POST /catalogue/upsert_draft_values - Add or change entries in the draft (batch)

request.description:
Each item is matched on `value_id` when given, else on `value_code`; unmatched items are added. Only fields present are changed. Labels, attributes, parent and sort order stay editable; a code can change (item with `value_id`) only for an entry that was never published — a published code is refused with `G2P-CAT-CODE-IMMUTABLE` (retire it and add a new entry instead). Upserting a retired code re-activates it. `attributes` are validated against the draft's attribute_schema, and `x-list-ref` codes must be ACTIVE values of the referenced list's version in effect (now, or at the draft's future effective_from) — never its draft: publish a referenced list first.

Edits only ever touch the open DRAFT (one per list / for geography); a draft is created from the highest published version when none is open. Published versions are immutable (enforced in Postgres).

Permission: `referenceData:edit`

item.name: POST /catalogue/get_geo_crosswalk - Map a unit across versions

request.description:
Follows the change events from `from_version` to `to_version` (default latest; may be earlier, to find predecessors) across any number of versions. Returns the unit's successors (SPLIT gives several, MERGE one, RECODE the new code; RENAME/REPARENT/BOUNDARY_CHANGE keep the unit) as they are in `to_version`, `unmapped` units (retired without successor / created without predecessor) and the `path` of events taken.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

item.name: POST /catalogue/get_geo_levels - Levels of a geography version

request.description:
Levels top-down (level_id, level_mnemonic, parent_level_id, display, display_i18n).

Version selection: `version` (number, `"latest"` — the default, the latest published version already in effect — or `"draft"`), `as_of` (date-time: the published version in effect then) or `release` (a catalogue release code). The response's `version` object says which version answered.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

`visibility` (private — the default — or public) and the optional licence (`licence_uri`, `licence_label`) of the geography. Administrative, not versioned.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

item.name: POST /catalogue/get_geo_unit - One unit, with its ancestors

request.description:
A unit of the selected version (retired ones too) and its ancestor chain.

Version selection: `version` (number, `"latest"` — the default, the latest published version already in effect — or `"draft"`), `as_of` (date-time: the published version in effect then) or `release` (a catalogue release code). The response's `version` object says which version answered.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

item.name: POST /catalogue/get_geo_units - Units of a geography version

request.description:
Units (unit_id = P-code, level_id, name, name_i18n, parent_unit_id, status, valid_from, valid_to), filtered by `level` (id or mnemonic), `parent_unit_id` ("" = roots), `search`; active only unless `include_retired`. Paged. GEO data policies apply.

Version selection: `version` (number, `"latest"` — the default, the latest published version already in effect — or `"draft"`), `as_of` (date-time: the published version in effect then) or `release` (a catalogue release code). The response's `version` object says which version answered.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

All geography versions, newest first, with status, effective_from, owner_org, country, active unit count and the boundary object key per level.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

item.name: POST /catalogue/update_geo_settings - Set the geography's visibility / licence

request.description:
Applied at once (not versioned); only fields present are changed, an empty licence field clears it. `visibility: "public"` lets the anonymous /public catalogue (when enabled) show the geography's PUBLISHED versions; drafts are never public. Logged as `geo.settings.updated`.

Permission: `geo:edit`

item.name: 07. Catalogue - Geography Drafts Workflow
item.description: Endpoints in group 07. Catalogue - Geography Drafts Workflow

item.name: POST /catalogue/approve_geo_draft - Approve and publish the geography draft (permission mode)

request.description:
Publishes the SUBMITTED version (immutable), stamps valid_from / valid_to on new and retired units and — if in effect — refreshes the legacy /geo tables in the same transaction. Maker ≠ checker. Disabled in awe mode.

Permission: `geo:publish`

Copies levels, units and boundary keys of the highest published version (or `copy_from_version`). Optional `change_note`, `effective_from` (e.g. new woredas from 2027-01-01), `owner_org`.

Permission: `geo:edit`

item.name: POST /catalogue/delete_geo_change - Remove a change event from the geography draft

request.description:
Only events of the open DRAFT.

Permission: `geo:edit`

Closes the open geography draft as DISCARDED (kept, so its number and boundary keys are never reused). Uploaded objects of the draft stay in the bucket under its own version's keys.

Permission: `geo:edit`

item.name: POST /catalogue/get_geo_boundary - Boundary GeoJSON of a level

request.description:
The object key of the level's boundary in the selected version (`geo/<country>/v<version>/<level>.geojson`, immutable once published; an unchanged level points at an earlier version's object), with `url` (when a public base URL is configured) and a `presigned_url`. With `stream: true` the GeoJSON itself is returned as application/geo+json.

Version selection: `version` (number, `"latest"` — the default, the latest published version already in effect — or `"draft"`), `as_of` (date-time: the published version in effect then) or `release` (a catalogue release code). The response's `version` object says which version answered.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

Events of the published versions in (`from_version`, `to_version`] — CREATE, RETIRE, RENAME, RECODE, SPLIT, MERGE, REPARENT, BOUNDARY_CHANGE with from_units (base version) and to_units (new version), effective_date, note, is_auto. `unit_id` filters to events naming it; `include_draft` adds the open draft's events.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

item.name: POST /catalogue/record_geo_change - Record a change event in the geography draft

request.description:
Lineage against the draft's base version. Rules: CREATE — to-units active in the draft and new; RETIRE — from-units active in base, retired in the draft; RENAME / REPARENT — one unit, same id, name / parent differs; RECODE — one old code (retired) to one new code (new), same level; SPLIT — one from-unit (retired, or kept as one of the parts) to ≥2 active to-units; MERGE — ≥2 from-units (retired, or the survivor) to one active unit; BOUNDARY_CHANGE — units active in both. A unit can end in only one RETIRE/SPLIT/MERGE/RECODE per version. Edit the units first, then record the event.

Permission: `geo:edit`

item.name: POST /catalogue/reject_geo_draft - Reject the geography draft (permission mode)

request.description:
Requires `decision_note`. Maker ≠ checker.

Permission: `geo:publish`

item.name: POST /catalogue/submit_geo_draft - Submit the geography draft for approval

request.description:
Validates levels, units and every recorded event, completes the lineage (auto CREATE / RETIRE / RENAME / REPARENT / BOUNDARY_CHANGE events for anything not covered, flagged is_auto) and moves the draft to SUBMITTED; in awe mode opens an AWE request (`awe_policy_key_geo`, artifact `master_data.geo_version`).

Permission: `geo:edit`

item.name: POST /catalogue/update_geo_draft - Set the geography draft's note / effective date / owner

request.description:
Only fields present are changed.

Permission: `geo:edit`

item.name: 08. Catalogue - Releases Management
item.description: Endpoints in group 08. Catalogue - Releases Management

request.description:
`release_code` (e.g. 2027.1), `title`, `note`.

Permission: `referenceData:edit`

Published releases cannot be deleted.

Permission: `referenceData:delete`

item.name: POST /catalogue/get_release - One release with its members

request.description:
`members: [{list_id, list_code, version_no}]` and `geo_version_no`.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

Named sets of list versions plus one geography version, for consumers that pin everything at once. Any versioned read accepts `release` to answer from a release's pins.

Permission: any authenticated caller.

Checks every member is published and that `x-list-ref` references between member lists resolve within the release's own pins. Maker ≠ checker (publisher ≠ creator and ≠ whoever last set the members). Immutable afterwards (enforced in Postgres).

Permission: `referenceData:publish`

item.name: POST /catalogue/set_release_members - Pin dataset versions and a geography version

request.description:
Only PUBLISHED versions can be members. `replace: true` (default) replaces all members; false adds / overwrites the given ones. `geo_version_no` sets the geography pin. DRAFT releases only.

Permission: `referenceData:edit`

Permission: `referenceData:delete`.

item.name: POST /attributes/delete_attribute_value - Retire an entry (in the draft)

request.description: Catalogue: this no longer changes published data. It edits the list's open DRAFT (creating one from the latest published version if needed); the change reaches the readers of /attributes/* only when the draft is submitted and approved (see /catalogue/submit_draft and /catalogue/approve_draft). item.name: 11. Samples API (Demo / Test)
item.description: Endpoints in group 11. Samples API (Demo / Test)

item.name: POST /samples/get_households - Sample households (testing and demos only)

request.description: **For testing and demos only; not for production use.** The sample households the country pack loaded, in `household_id` order, with their head, size, dwelling and amenities (codes of the pack's datasets) and location. Optional filters: `geo_pcode`, `country`. Paged with `pagination_request` (`page_size`, `current_page`; default 1000 per page); `response_body.pagination_response` carries `number_of_items` and `number_of_pages`. Empty unless the deployment loaded the country pack's samples (`--load samples`). Permission: any authenticated caller.

item.name: POST /samples/get_individuals - Sample people (testing and demos only)

request.description: **For testing and demos only; not for production use.** Sample people are made-up demo data, not reference data: they are not versioned or approved, and a production deployment should not load them. The sample individuals the country pack loaded, in `individual_id` order: who they are (names, gender, birth date, national id, phone), where they live (`geo_pcode`, a unit of the geography, plus `address_parts` below the lowest level and coordinates) and coded facts (entries of the pack's datasets). Registries seed their sample records from these, so one set of people populates every registry of the deployment. Optional filters: `household_id`, `geo_pcode`, `country`. Paged with `pagination_request` (`page_size`, `current_page`; default 1000 per page); `response_body.pagination_response` carries `number_of_items` and `number_of_pages`. Empty unless the deployment loaded the country pack's samples (`--load samples`). Permission: any authenticated caller.

Called by the Approval Workflow Engine (awe mode). Authenticated by HMAC, not JWT: `X-Approval-Signature: sha256=HMAC_SHA256(secret, "<X-Approval-Timestamp>." + body)`, with `X-Approval-Timestamp` (unix seconds) and `X-Approval-Event-Id`. Body: AWE WebhookEvent (`event_id, event_type, request_id, artifact_type, artifact_id, status, stage_order, actor, occurred_at`). `request_approved` publishes the submitted version (artifact `master_data.list_version` `<list_id>:<version_no>`, or `master_data.geo_version` `geography:<version_no>`); `request_rejected` / `request_cancelled` reject it. Idempotent on event_id. 401 on a bad signature, 422 when the event cannot be applied.
